name: JARVIS-1 (Open-World Multi-task Agents with Memory-Augmented Multimodal Language Models)
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence (TPAMI), vol. 47, pp. 1894-1907, 2024 (peer-reviewed journal; DOI 10.1109/TPAMI.2024.3511593; DBLP journals/pami/WangCLJHZLHZYML25). Preprint: arXiv:2311.05997 (v1 10 Nov 2023, v3 30 Nov 2023; cs.AI).

code_url: https://github.com/CraftJarvis/JARVIS-1 (official code, 395 stars; only offline_evaluation with fixed memory and the language-model part released; multimodal descriptor/retrieval and online learning.py with growing memory marked 'Coming Soon'). Project page: https://craftjarvis.org/JARVIS-1 (also https://craftjarvis-jarvis1.github.io/).
maintained_repo_url: N/A - no separately maintained leaderboard/paper-list repo. The CraftJarvis org (https://github.com/CraftJarvis) hosts related projects (STEVE-1 is external; MC-TextWorld, MCU/Minecraft Universe Benchmark by Lin et al. 2023a) but no continuously-updated tracking list specific to JARVIS-1.
task_domain: Embodied / open-world decision-making and long-horizon planning: an MLM-based generalist agent that perceives multimodal input (RGB visual observations + textual human instructions), generates plans, and performs human-like embodied control (mouse/keyboard) in the open-world Minecraft universe. High-level memory-augmented MLM planner + low-level goal-conditioned controller (STEVE-1). Not QA; interactive embodied agentic decision-making with life-long learning.
problem_setting: Interactive, single-agent embodied decision-making in Minecraft 1.16.5 survival mode (hybrid MineRL + MCP-Reborn environment), running at 20 fps. The agent uses a human-like observation space (640x360 ego-centric RGB pov plus auxiliary location/inventory/equipment/event info) and a human-like action space (keypresses, mouse yaw/pitch, plus abstracted craft/smelt/equip functional actions as in MineDojo). Default evaluation starts in survival mode with an empty inventory (some intermediate groups start with an iron_axe) and a random spawn; a task succeeds if the target object is obtained within a Max.Steps budget (12k-72k steps). Train-free / no gradient update: planning is via a frozen pre-trained MLM (GPT-3.5/GPT-4 as the language part chained with frozen MineCLIP for vision) augmented with a retrievable multimodal memory built and grown in-context. Supervision: no imitation/RL fine-tuning of the planner; the agent acquires experiences via self-instruct exploration and stores only SUCCESSFUL trajectories. Multiple JARVIS-1 instances run in parallel (speculative/distributed execution) sharing one centralized memory during the learning stage, but the deployed agent is single-agent. (The low-level controller STEVE-1 is itself pre-trained via VPT+MineCLIP; the GPT/LLM is accessed via OpenAI API.)
what_is_retrieved: EXPERIENCES: past successful interactive planning experiences (multimodal trajectory entries) from the agent's own gameplay. Each retrieved entry is a key-value record whose key is multimodal (task instruction + the visual observation/situation when the entry was created) and whose value is the successfully executed plan (the goal sequence). Retrieved plans are injected as in-context demonstration references to augment current planning. (Only successful trajectories are stored.)
retrieval_grounding: GROWING / episodic memory the agent writes (with a self-instruct life-long-learning growth mechanism). The retrievable store is the agent's own multimodal memory of past successful planning experiences, built by self-exploration and continuously expanded during gameplay - not a static external document corpus. Pretrained world knowledge also informs planning, but it lives inside the frozen MLM weights, not in the retrievable index. Mildly hybrid in that situation captioning uses ~1000 internet-collected Minecraft text snippets matched by MineCLIP, but the RETRIEVAL store used for retrieval-augmented planning is the growing experience memory.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k ranking with a per-sub-goal selection structure. The retriever returns the plan of the top-k candidate entries (Eq. 1 sum over top-k; Eq. 2 ranks candidates by visual-state similarity). In query generation, only the top entry of EACH decomposed sub-goal is retrieved (per Fig. 5 caption), so effectively a small per-sub-goal top-1 union rather than a single global ranked list. The objective is relevance-driven retrieval of useful reference plans, not recovery of a provably complete minimal set. [uncertain on the exact numeric k]
cbr_cycle_coverage: [Retrieve: yes, Reuse: yes, Revise: partial, Retain: yes (success-only)]. Retrieve: multimodal-query similarity retrieval of relevant past plans. Reuse: retrieved plans injected as in-context demonstration references to produce the current plan. Revise: at the case level NO (retrieved plans are not edited); but the agent's overall plan is revised via interactive planning (self-check before execution + self-explain/re-plan on environment feedback), so plan-level revision exists. Retain: successful trajectories (task + state + plan) are written back to memory.
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The paper does NOT frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner. It explicitly frames the mechanism as retrieval-augmented generation (RAG; cites Lewis et al. 2020, Mao et al. 2020) over a multimodal experience memory, plus in-context life-long learning, self-instruct, and self-reflection (Reflexion/self-debugging). It nonetheless realizes Retrieve/Reuse/Retain CBR-like mechanisms (plus plan-level revise) under the RAG/memory framing.
retrieval_unit: Full trajectory / case (problem-solution). The retrieved unit is a stored experience entry = a successful planning trajectory encoded as a dict with keys {task, state, plan}: the task goal, the agent state (visual observation + symbolic info: inventory, location, etc.) at planning time, and the actual executed goal sequence (plan). The injected content is the plan (an ordered list of short-horizon goals / mine-craft-smelt steps). So the unit is a (task+situation -> plan) case.
index_source: Growing, agent-written memory; online/test-time-induced. The memory is built non-parametrically by the agent itself: during a learning stage JARVIS-1 explores via self-instruct curricula, executes plans, and stores all SUCCESSFUL trajectory experiences; the store keeps growing throughout gameplay (life-long learning) without gradient updates. Not an offline static corpus. Distributed self-improve fills a shared centralized memory in parallel.
index_structure_topology: Flat key-value (metadata/context-keyed) experience list. The memory is a list of dictionaries, each {task, state, plan}; keys are MULTIMODAL (task text + visual state). Retrieval is text-key filtering (CLIP text similarity above a confidence threshold) followed by visual-state similarity ranking. No knowledge graph or hierarchical category index; the implicit structure is per-sub-goal grouping at query time (retrieve top entry for each decomposed sub-goal). Same task may have multiple entries keyed by different observations/situations.
retriever_type: Dense / embedding-similarity (off-the-shelf CLIP/MineCLIP), with LLM-as-query-generator. Two stages: (1) text retrieval - CLIP text encoder embeds the textual query and each entry's task key, keeping entries above a similarity confidence threshold; (2) visual rerank - MineCLIP/CLIP visual encoder computes visual-state similarity between query observation and candidate states (Eq. 2) to sort candidates. No BM25, no trained dense retriever; the LLM/MLM reasons to GENERATE the queries (backward sub-goal search) but the matching itself is frozen-encoder cosine similarity.
retriever_learning_signal: None (off-the-shelf). The retriever uses frozen pre-trained encoders: CLIP text encoder for the textual task key and MineCLIP/CLIP visual encoder for the visual state, with a similarity confidence threshold. No contrastive training on similarity labels, no LM-feedback, no preference/RL training of the retriever. Improvement over time comes from a GROWING memory (more/better stored experiences), not from training the retriever. (MineCLIP is pre-trained on YouTube video-text pairs; not fine-tuned here.)
query_construction: Query generation via LLM reasoning + visual augmentation. Given the task and current observation, the MLM reasons backward (think-backward) to decompose the instruction into the needed intermediate sub-goals / related tasks (bounded search depth), e.g. 'craft 1 enchanting table' -> 'obtain book/diamond/obsidian with empty inventory'. Each sub-goal that exists in memory becomes a TEXTUAL query, which is then concatenated with the agent's current VISUAL observation to form a MULTIMODAL query (situation-aware). So queries are decomposed/synthetic sub-goal queries, not the raw instruction alone.
query_granularity: Both task-level and step/sub-goal-level (two-level). The task instruction is decomposed by reasoning into multiple sub-goal queries; retrieval is performed per sub-goal (and conditioned on the current visual state), and the current visual situation grounds the query at the state level. Effectively a two-level retrieval: reason to sub-goals (decomposition) then retrieve situation-grounded plans per sub-goal.
when_to_retrieve: One-shot at the start of (re)planning, repeated across the interactive-planning loop. Retrieval is triggered when JARVIS-1 plans (and when it re-plans after a failure). It is not token-confidence/uncertainty-triggered nor a learned router; retrieval happens at each planning event. Because the interactive planner re-plans on self-check/self-explain feedback, retrieval can recur per re-plan round (typically 2-3 rounds vs DEPS's 6+).
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed/event-driven: retrieval fires at each planning and re-planning event in the control loop. A (re)plan is invoked (a) at task start, (b) on self-check finding a predicted precondition violation before execution, or (c) on a runtime execution error that triggers self-explain -> re-plan. There is no token-confidence / attention-uncertainty / learned-complexity-classifier / reflection-token trigger for retrieval; retrieval is bound to the planner being called.
reranking: Yes - a two-stage similarity rerank (not a learned cross-encoder). Stage 1: CLIP text-key similarity filters candidates above a confidence threshold. Stage 2: the surviving candidates are re-ranked by MineCLIP/CLIP VISUAL-state similarity between the query observation and each candidate's stored state (Eq. 2), and the top-k plans are returned (only the top entry per sub-goal is kept). No cross-encoder / RRF / instruction-tuned reranker.
retrieved_context_refinement: Rerank + selection (situation-aware filtering). Refinement is the text-threshold filter then visual-similarity rerank, plus keeping only the top entry per decomposed sub-goal so the prompt holds a small set of the most situation-relevant reference plans. No decompose-then-recompose of retrieved content, no reason-in-documents distillation, no explicit distractor-removal module, no compression of stored plans.
tool_document_engineering: N/A - no tool/API description store is indexed. Low-level skills are executed by a single fixed controller (STEVE-1) plus environment craft/smelt/equip primitives; there are no retrievable tool docstrings to engineer.
index_content_separation: Partial. The text task-key is used for a cheap first-stage filter before the heavier visual-state similarity comparison on candidates only, which separates a lightweight text index from costlier multimodal scoring. But there is no formal progressive-disclosure / SOP-index-then-content protocol; the full {task,state,plan} entry is stored together.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A as a tool-retrieval system. The experience memory is a live, incrementally-growing list updated during gameplay, but there is no RapidAPI/REST/MCP/function-calling tool protocol. The agent acts via the human-like MineRL/MCP-Reborn interface (keyboard/mouse) plus abstracted craft/smelt actions; plans are emitted as Python-like mine/craft/smelt pseudo-code parsed into goals.
tool_dependency_awareness: Not for tools, but craft/mine PRECONDITIONS are reasoned about (not retrieved as a dependency graph). JARVIS-1 handles item prerequisites (e.g. stone_pickaxe needed before mining iron_ore; crafting_table needed for certain recipes) via LLM self-check precondition simulation and self-explain error explanation, and via backward sub-goal decomposition - i.e. dependency awareness is implemented in the reasoning/planner, not via an explicit retrievable dependency/bipartite graph.
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation (in-context). Retrieved reference plans z are inserted into the MLM planner prompt alongside the task instruction and textual situation descriptions (Eq. 1: p(y|x) ~ sum_z p_eta(z|x) p_theta(y|x,z)); the planner then produces the current plan grounded in both its pretrained knowledge and these retrieved experiences. No weight updates (train-free, in-context life-long learning). The retrieved plans serve as demonstration exemplars / reference templates the planner adapts to the current situation.
planning_integration: Retrieve-then-plan, embedded in a closed-loop interactive planning framework. Pipeline: (1) on a task+observation, the MLM generates a multimodal query (backward sub-goal reasoning) and retrieves relevant past plans; (2) the memory-augmented MLM produces a plan of K short-horizon goals g1..gK; (3) self-check simulates the plan and fixes precondition bugs before execution; (4) the controller (STEVE-1) executes goals; (5) on execution failure, self-explain reasons about the error and triggers re-planning (which retrieves again). So retrieval supplies one-shot exemplars at each (re)plan time inside an interleaved self-check / self-explain re-planning loop; no MCTS/tree search.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-plan / per-re-plan-round within a rollout (sub-goal-level on the query side). Retrieval and reasoning are woven in at planning events: backward reasoning decomposes the task into sub-goals (per-sub-goal retrieval), a plan is generated, then self-check / self-explain feedback triggers further re-plan-with-retrieval rounds (typically 2-3). It is NOT per-CoT-token or per-low-level-action; it is per planning round / per sub-goal query.
adaptation_mechanism: LLM-prompted adaptation + execution-feedback-driven plan revision. Retrieved plans are used as in-context reference exemplars and the MLM adapts them to the current situation/inventory rather than copying verbatim; the overall plan is further revised through self-check (pre-execution precondition simulation) and self-explain (post-failure error reasoning -> re-plan). No RL-reuse-finetuning and no latent adaptation; adaptation is prompt-based plus interactive feedback.
retrieved_item_representation: Free-text / structured plan (goal sequence). What is injected is the stored successful PLAN - an ordered sequence of short-horizon mine/craft/smelt goals (rendered as Python-like pseudo-code with step comments, e.g. mine({'log':3}); craft({'planks':12},{'log':3})). It is a structured procedural plan, not a raw pixel trajectory, not an executable compiled program/skill, not latent tokens, and not a distilled natural-language strategy.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Reusable plan / procedure grounded to a situation - mid-level. The retrieved unit is a concrete past successful plan (ordered sub-goal sequence) keyed by a specific task+situation, i.e. a situated procedural reference, more abstract than a raw action trajectory but more concrete than a distilled free-text strategy or a generalized workflow/rule. It is a single successful demonstration plan per retrieved case.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Interactive self-verification rather than retriever-side training. Robustness against bad plans/contexts comes from: (1) success-only memory (only verified successful trajectories are stored, so retrieved references are correct plans); (2) self-check precondition simulation before execution to catch flawed plans upfront; (3) self-explain on environment feedback to detect/locate execution errors and re-plan; (4) situation-aware multimodal retrieval (visual-state rerank + confidence threshold) to keep references relevant to the current situation. No retriever-aware/distractor-aware SFT and no separate relevance evaluator over retrieved items.
memory_type: Episodic multimodal memory (key-value experience store of successful planning trajectories: keys = task+visual situation, values = executed plans). Non-parametric / in-context (no skill-library of programs, no graph, no latent memory). Pretrained semantic knowledge resides in the frozen MLM, separate from this episodic store.
write_back: True. Every SUCCESSFUL trajectory experience is written to memory as a dict {task, state (visual obs + symbolic info at completion), plan (executed goal sequence)}. New entries are added during both the self-instruct learning stage and ongoing gameplay.
online_growth: True. The memory grows during deployment/gameplay (life-long learning): starting from a small/seed memory, JARVIS-1 self-instructs exploration curricula and accumulates successful trajectories; success rates rise with memory size (Fig. 7) and with longer game-playing time (e.g. ObtainDiamondPickaxe 6.2% at 20 min -> 12.5% at 60 min). After 4 epochs of learning across all task sets, the memory held 425 successful trajectories. The growing memory is the only online code (online_evaluation/learning.py) not yet released as of the repo.
write_back_trigger: On-success only. A trajectory is written back to memory only when the task/plan is SUCCESSFULLY executed (the memory 'records every successful trajectory experience'). Failures are used transiently for self-explain/re-planning within the episode but are NOT stored as memory entries. Writes are not human-validated; they are gated by environment-confirmed task success.
failure_experience_usage: Success-only storage; failures used only transiently in-loop. Failed plans are leveraged immediately via self-explain (error explanation + re-plan) to recover within the current episode, but failure/negative experiences are NOT stored or retrieved from the multimodal memory. (This success-only design is exactly what the later Optimus-1 paper contrasts against by adding failure cases to its experience pool.)
memory_evolution_update: Append-only (with situation-keyed duplicates allowed). Successful trajectories are appended to the memory list; the same task can have multiple entries differing in observation/plan (situated). No dedup-merge, delta-update, refine-overwrite, or forget-prune of stored entries is described (the learning experiments grow memory monotonically up to a capacity). [uncertain on any eviction/capacity-cap policy]
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Case selection is fixed similarity top-k (CLIP text-threshold filter + MineCLIP visual-similarity rerank, Eq. 2), with LLM-reasoned query generation. There is no learned/RL-optimized retrieval policy (no M-MDP soft Q-learning, no trained retriever). The MLM only generates queries; matching is frozen-encoder cosine similarity.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: Yes, within the same framework (shared centralized memory across parallel homogeneous instances). During self-improve/learning, multiple JARVIS-1 agents run in parallel in different environments (speculative/distributed execution) and collect experiences into one shared centralized memory, accelerating memory growth. The memory is also backbone-swappable (ChatGPT / GPT-4 / fine-tuned LLaMA2-13B all use the same memory). It is not a cooperative multi-agent deployment nor sharing across heterogeneous agent frameworks; sharing is across parallel copies of JARVIS-1 / interchangeable LM backbones.
benchmarks: Minecraft, 200+ tasks selected from the Minecraft Universe Benchmark / MCU (Lin et al. 2023a), grouped into 11 categories: Wood (34), Wood-Variants (43), Stone (10), Iron (22), Gold (9), Diamond (7), Redstone (7), Blocks (15), Armor (17), Decoration (17), Food (9); evaluated in Minecraft 1.16.5 survival mode (hybrid MineRL + MCP-Reborn), >=30 seeds per task (key items like diamond_pickaxe/diamond evaluated 300-728 times). Flagship long-horizon challenge: ObtainDiamondPickaxe (also extended to 60-minute / 72000-step gameplay).
benchmark_family: Embodied / open-world (Minecraft) under the survey's embodied family (ALFWorld/ScienceWorld/VirtualHome/Minecraft). Long-horizon crafting/mining decision-making with human-like low-level visuomotor control.
baselines: LLM/MLM multi-task instruction-following planners: Instruct GPT (Huang et al. 2022a / Ouyang et al. 2022, plan-once), ReAct (Yao et al. 2022, reason-before-act), Inner Monologue (Huang et al. 2022b, feedback re-planning), and DEPS (Wang et al. 2023b, Describe-Explain-Plan-Select interactive planning, the strongest prior baseline) - all reproduced to Minecraft. For the long-horizon ObtainDiamondPickaxe challenge: VPT / VPT-RL (Baker et al. 2022, RL-finetuned over 1.4M episodes), STEVE-1 (Lifshitz et al. 2023, controller), DEPS, and a human-player baseline (10-min gameplay, ~15% diamond / ~12% diamond pickaxe). LM ablations compare ChatGPT, GPT-4, pre-trained LLaMA2-70B, and fine-tuned LLaMA2-13B.
key_metrics: Average task Success Rate (SR, %) per task group (reported as mean +/- variance), at least 30 seeds per task; for the long-horizon study, SR (% episodes) of obtaining the diamond pickaxe and intermediate milestone items over game-playing time (steps/minutes), plus efficiency proxies (rounds of re-planning, LLM tokens/thinking time). Primary headline metric is SR.
headline_result: On ObtainDiamondPickaxe, JARVIS-1 surpasses the prior state-of-the-art by ~5x: 6.22% SR within 20 minutes (24k steps) vs VPT-RL's ~2.5% (>2x VPT directly; '5x the reliability of current SOTA' in the abstract vs DEPS ~0.59-2.5%); extending gameplay to 60 minutes (72k steps) raises JARVIS-1 to 12.5% (vs human ~12% in 10 min). On the 200+ task benchmark JARVIS-1 is best in every group, e.g. group-AVG SR vs DEPS: Wood 88.84 vs 80.23, Stone 88.69 vs 69.27, Iron 34.63 vs 16.92, Gold 6.85 vs 2.20, Diamond 8.99 vs 2.42 (~3x on diamond tasks), Redstone 17.51 vs 6.02. It is described as the most general Minecraft agent, completing 200+ tasks with human-like observation/action spaces.
ablations: (1) Architecture/challenge ablations (Fig. 2): situation-aware planning, interactive planning, and memory each substantially raise SR, with gains growing as task complexity increases (Stone->Iron->Diamond); cross-task memory transfer (Fig. 2 Right) shows experiences on related tasks (e.g. DiamondAxe) boost a target task (DiamondPickaxe). (2) LM backbone (Fig. 6 / Table 6): with memory, ChatGPT ~= GPT-4 SR; pre-trained LLaMA2-70B is poor on Minecraft, but fine-tuned LLaMA2-13B matches ChatGPT. (3) Memory size / self-improve (Fig. 7): SR on key tech-tree items rises with memory size, reaching 425 stored successful trajectories after 4 learning epochs. (4) Retrieval method (Fig. 8): Text-Memory < Text-Memory+Reasoning < Multimodal-Memory+Reasoning - reasoning before retrieval improves retrieval accuracy, and multimodal (vision+symbolic) retrieval beats text-only. (5) Long-horizon self-improve curriculum (Fig. 9): GPT-generated curriculum > human-written > random; SR keeps rising with longer gameplay (6.2%->12.5%) whereas VPT-RL is flat (2.5%->3%).
evaluation_decoupling: No. Only end-to-end task SR (and efficiency proxies) are reported. Intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k / nDCG / completeness) are NOT reported separately; retrieval quality is assessed indirectly via the Fig. 8 retrieval-method ablation on downstream SR ('reasoning before retrieval improves retrieval accuracy', measured through task performance).
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome (final task SR), with some process/efficiency signals: number of re-planning rounds (JARVIS-1 ~2-3 vs DEPS 6+), LLM token / thinking-time savings, and milestone-item SR curves over time (Fig. 9 Right) that track intermediate progress on the diamond-pickaxe tech tree. No reasoning-faithfulness or step-wise retrieval-accuracy metric is scored directly.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Efficiency is a stated advantage. JARVIS-1 typically needs only 2-3 rounds of re-planning to produce a correct executable plan vs DEPS's 6+, saving substantial LLM tokens and thinking time and leaving more steps/tokens for environment uncertainty. Training-free / no gradient update (in-context life-long learning) avoids RL fine-tuning cost (contrast: VPT-RL needs 1.4M episodes). Distributed self-improve with shared memory and speculative execution accelerates experience collection. Compute: experiments use OpenAI API for the LM and GPU for STEVE-1/MineCLIP; NVIDIA GPU support acknowledged. [uncertain on exact API/$ cost and total compute]
context_budget_and_selection_count: Small reranked-then-truncated set: top-k candidate plans returned (Eq. 1 top-k), keeping only the top entry of each decomposed sub-goal; CLIP text-similarity above a confidence threshold gates candidates, then visual-state similarity ranks them. Re-planning is bounded (typically 2-3 rounds) and the backward sub-goal search depth is bounded for efficiency. No explicit token-budget cap is reported; selection is threshold + per-sub-goal-top-1 driven. [uncertain on exact k, similarity threshold, and search-depth values]
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A - JARVIS-1 is a method/agent paper, not a survey or taxonomy.
benchmark_construction_and_size: Evaluation set of 200+ tasks selected from the Minecraft Universe Benchmark / MCU (Lin et al. 2023a), grouped into 11 recommended-category groups (sizes: Wood 34, Wood-Var 43, Stone 10, Iron 22, Gold 9, Diamond 7, Redstone 7, Blocks 15, Armor 17, Decoration 17, Food 9). Tasks target obtainable overworld items; success is auto-verifiable from Minecraft inventory/environment feedback; Max.Steps per task set to human completion time (12k-72k steps); each task run >=30 times across different seeds (diamond_pickaxe 692 times, diamond 728 times). Difficulty signaled by best-system SR collapsing along the tech tree (e.g. Diamond group AVG only 8.99% for JARVIS-1, single ObtainDiamondPickaxe 6.22%-12.5%, leaving a large gap to mastery).
builds_on: DEPS (Wang et al. 2023b, interactive Describe-Explain-Plan-Select planning - direct predecessor for the interactive planning framework); STEVE-1 (Lifshitz et al. 2023, used directly as the goal-conditioned low-level controller); MineCLIP (Fan et al. 2022 / MineDojo, chained with the LLM to form the MLM, also the frozen visual encoder/retriever); VPT (Baker et al. 2022, underlying foundation policy & action/observation interface); RAG (Lewis et al. 2020; Mao et al. 2020, retrieval-augmented generation formulation); Self-Instruct (Wang et al. 2022, curriculum generation); Reflexion (Shinn et al. 2023, self-explain) and self-debugging (Chen et al. 2023, self-check); GPT-3.5/GPT-4 and LLaMA2 (planner LMs); MineRL + MCP-Reborn (environment); MCU/Minecraft Universe Benchmark (Lin et al. 2023a). Same CraftJarvis group lineage from DEPS.
contrasts_with: DEPS (Wang et al. 2023b - no memory, cannot learn from cross-task experience, limited re-planning rounds; JARVIS-1 adds multimodal memory and life-long learning, ~3x on diamond tasks with 2-3 vs 6+ re-plan rounds); GITM/Ghost-in-the-Minecraft (Zhu et al. 2023) and Voyager (Wang et al. 2023a) - text-only memory / text-based knowledge and custom non-human interfaces (MineDojo high-level APIs / code skills); JARVIS-1 uses MULTIMODAL memory + human-like raw-pixel observation and mouse/keyboard action spaces; ReAct / Inner Monologue / Instruct-GPT (no memory, weaker on long-horizon); VPT / VPT-RL (RL-finetuned, flat improvement over time, cannot follow instructions / re-plan on tool breakage). Notably success-only memory contrasts with later Optimus-1 (which adds failure cases and experience summarization).
lineage: Group F (decision-making / memory / RL) at the intersection of retrieval-augmented planning and experiential episodic-memory agents. Lineage: video/IL+RL Minecraft policies (VPT, MineCLIP, STEVE-1) -> LLM-planner agents (Inner Monologue, DEPS, Voyager, GITM) -> JARVIS-1, which adds a GROWING multimodal episodic memory retrieved (reasoning + multimodal similarity) to augment a frozen-MLM planner for life-long open-world planning. Direct successor: Optimus-1 (Li et al. 2024, NeurIPS) which builds on and contrasts with JARVIS-1 by adding a hierarchical directed knowledge graph (HDKG) and an abstracted multimodal experience pool (AMEP) with success+failure cases; further Optimus-2/Optimus-3.
